allerhønsegårds: utterly foolish/lowly (comic superlative, lit. 'best of the henyard')
ave: discipline (holde i ave = to keep in check)
bens: of leg (til bens = on foot / fast runner)
droge: traveled / drew (archaic plural past tense of drage)
folkemunde: popular speech (i folkemunde = as commonly said)
forvilde: to lead astray / to get lost
gab: mouth / gap (of an animal), or yawn
glandsen: the glow / luster (old spelling of glansen)
glaskorn: glass shard / splinter (from the troll mirror)
havkatten: the sea cat (catfish / mythical sea creature)
herreblade: face cards (kings, in a card deck)
herremand: country squire / lord of the manor
herskabet: the master and mistress / the gentry
hoppe: to hop / to jump; mare (female horse)
istand: able to (i stand til = capable of)
kede: to bore / kede sig = to be bored
muk: a sound / peep (sige et muk = to not say a word)
passe: to fit / to take care of
rendestensbrættet: the gutter board (over a street drain)
sade: sat (archaic plural past tense of sidde)
sengs: bed (in 'gå til sengs', go to bed)
skøtte: to look after / to tend to
sloge: struck / hit (archaic plural past tense of slå)
udkomme: to be published / to come out
von: von (German preposition, part of a name)
